scope: Survey only. Same-utterance Local256, Base512, Gap3x512 and availability; preserve OSRAM read/write queries, Flat and task loss. Admissible means a distinct migration hypothesis, not validated benefit or training authorization.
latest_screening: Re-screened for the user's suitable-40 shortlist, not the earlier numerical survey80 target. Four admissible complete mechanisms are retained: PrediNet, Soft MoE, SCL and ESBN. Three conditional records are excluded from the recommended count; four rejected records are audit trails, not proposed experiments. This lane intentionally falls short of 6–8 rather than pad with long-sequence methods or weak operator wrappers.
screening_notes: CoRelNet paper §4 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.05056) reduces to normalized pairwise dot products followed by an MLP, too close to the excluded pair-dot wrapper. Author repository README was found but method code was not inspected; not counted.

Intention is paper-method verified but no author implementation was located. The explicitly unofficial Eliyas0007/Pytorch-Intention implementation was inspected only as a warning: unconstrained alpha, inverse and an added softmax are not a sufficient author-source audit.

candidates.title: The Scattering Compositional Learner: Discovering Objects, Attributes, Relationships in Analogical Reasoning
candidates.source_evidence: Paper §3.1 inspected: split/share/merge constructs every object-to-attribute and attribute-to-relation composition with sharing across groups. Actual author files read: analogy/nn/modules/shared_group_mlp.py SharedGroupMLP.__init__/forward (lines 64–122), analogy/nn/visual_model.py Visual2Symbolic (lines 81–110), analogy/nn/symbolic_model.py AnalogyModel (lines 73–93 and forward), analogy/nn/model.py symbolic_beta=0.0 and compute_symbolic_loss returning None when beta is zero (lines 183–185). The paper's compositionality evaluation and optional symbolic supervision are not necessary to the task-only source model.
candidates.mechanism: A bank of object/facet representations is split into groups; the same bank of attribute functions acts on every group; merged outputs are regrouped across inputs so the same relation-function bank acts on every object–attribute combination. Retain the complete Cartesian set of learned compositions rather than selecting one route.
candidates.osram_mapping: Treat the five fixed roles as inputs, not image locations. Align dimensions and derive a small learned facet bank per available role; apply shared attribute maps to every facet; regroup matching facets/attributes across the five roles, pass availability alongside them, and apply a shared relation bank. Decode the complete compositional feature bank to masked raw-slot residuals before unchanged Flat. Remove source answer-candidate enumeration and image CNN, not the two split/share/merge stages. Use only original task loss, with symbolic_beta absent/zero.
candidates.substantive_difference: Graph diffusion scattering uses multiscale graph filters; SCL learns object/attribute/relation maps with Cartesian composition and cross-group weight sharing. Neural Interpreter selects module routes; SCL evaluates all factor combinations. NLM reasons across arities and quantifiers; SCL shares maps along factor axes. Compositional Attention recombines search and value heads, not two nested shared function banks. A single grouped MLP or token mixer is not a faithful SCL candidate.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Reusable attribute and relation maps could compare the same evidence property across Local/Base/Gap without learning an unrelated comparator for each role pair, a relevant inductive bias even for five fixed roles.
risks: The role vectors have no annotated objects; learned facets are latent feature groups, not physical objects.
Facets may fail to align across roles or collapse; keep the factor counts small.
Mask missing values before facet formation and supply mask to relation maps; do not create missing evidence or use symbolic ground-truth supervision.
The source's analogy candidate head is excluded; its replacement is a task adapter, so benefit remains a migration hypothesis.

candidates.title: Emergent Symbols through Binding in External Memory
candidates.source_evidence: Paper §3.2 Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.3.3 inspected. Author models/ESBN.py read in full (123 lines): per-forward empty M_k/M_v lists and zero LSTM state; sensory-value similarity; softmax retrieval weights and separate sigmoid confidence; gated retrieval of concatenated stored key/confidence; ReLU controller-generated key writes and sensory value appends; final controller step. Correct author branch is main, not master. Optional temporal context normalization is separable from the key/value-binding architecture.
candidates.mechanism: Keep sensory values and controller-generated abstract keys in separate temporary lists. Current sensory input addresses old values, but returns the corresponding abstract key and match confidence. The controller sees only this retrieved symbolic record, not the sensory vector, and emits the next abstract key; append its binding to the current sensory value. This indirect value-to-key interface is the central representational bottleneck.
candidates.osram_mapping: Traverse aligned Local/Base/Gap vectors in fixed semantic order inside one adapter call. Initialize both lists and controller state anew for every utterance; unavailable steps perform no read, write or controller update. Use feature-derived values, retrieve only earlier available evidence bindings, perform the final read-consumption step, and decode the resulting symbolic summary to masked slot residuals before existing Flat. These forward-local differentiable lists are not a dataset/sample cache, missing-value store or replacement for OSRAM memory. Keep OSRAM queries and writes unchanged; omit optional temporal normalization if active-count edge cases make it unsuitable.
candidates.substantive_difference: DAT associates evidence with a learned symbol library in relational attention; ESBN creates new controller-derived bindings inside each forward and enforces sensory/controller stream separation. NPS updates entities using selected rules; ESBN exposes only an indirectly retrieved symbol/confidence to its controller. OSRAM's delta-rule matrix is not this append-only sensory-key binding list, and is neither replaced nor queried differently. PrediNet emits pair predicates in parallel, whereas ESBN induces a sequential symbol state through binding indirection.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: The symbolic-controller bottleneck could represent agreement/repetition among a few heterogeneous evidence roles while reducing dependence on their absolute embedding coordinates; source tasks already involve small object collections, so no long-sequence premise is needed.
risks: Fixed traversal creates order asymmetry; report the semantic order and do not select it using test results.
With one active role there is no earlier binding to retrieve; source zero-read behavior must remain finite.
Passing sensory vectors directly into the controller or persisting lists across utterances invalidates the claimed migration.
A scalar confidence alone is not the candidate; dual lists, controller-generated keys, indirect retrieval and final controller update must all remain.

candidates.title: Exploring the Space of Key-Value-Query Models with Intention
candidates.source_evidence: Paper §3 and §3.1 Eq.(1) inspected: learned key/value/query embeddings, regularized inverse Gram least-squares map, optional learned map e_w, and query evaluation. Author implementation was not located despite targeted searches. https://github.com/Eliyas0007/Pytorch-Intention explicitly labels itself unofficial; its Intention.py was read but is not accepted as author-code evidence. Do not describe this card as paper-plus-author-code verified.
candidates.mechanism: Infer a within-example operator W=e_w[(K^T K+alpha I)^(-1)K^T V] and evaluate QW. The Gram solve jointly accounts for correlations among all available keys rather than computing independently normalized attention scores. Use a stable regularized solve; a dual form can keep the inversion at the number of active roles.
candidates.osram_mapping: K and V are learned transforms of the same utterance's available Local/Base/Gap vectors, not labels or target samples. Adapter-internal fixed-role Q reads a batch-fitted operator and decodes residuals before unchanged Flat. Mask active rows before constructing the solve, constrain alpha positive, and do not alter OSRAM query tensors. This is an algebraic layer trained through the existing task loss, not an auxiliary regression objective.
candidates.substantive_difference: The proposed distinction is an exact regularized, jointly correlation-corrected KVQ operator inferred from all current evidence rows. A kernel similarity alone does not solve the Gram system; LISTA unrolls sparse-code inference; OSRAM delta updates are a recurrence on the pre-existing memory. Nevertheless, author-code fidelity and a closer source/local-equation audit are still required before this can count.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: The inverse Gram factor may avoid counting highly redundant Base/Gap evidence multiple times while retaining components supplied by a distinct Local signal; this directly concerns few correlated roles rather than sequence scaling.
risks: Author implementation missing: paper-only conditional candidate, excluded from recommended count.
Ill-conditioned or nearly collinear role embeddings require positive regularization and stable solves.
Values must be feature embeddings, never supervised target labels.
Do not split softmax/kernel variants into multiple candidates or substitute the unofficial implementation without equation verification.

candidates.title: Large Memory Layers with Product Keys
candidates.source_evidence: Paper §3.1–3.2 inspected: split lookup query, two learned sub-key dictionaries, Cartesian candidate scores, exact global top-k, learned value table. Author code HashingMemoryProduct._get_indices and HashingMemoryProductFast._get_indices (raw file lines 468–618) inspected, including subquery top-k, additive Cartesian scores and gathered indices. Initial guessed src/model path returned 404; corrected xlm/model path actually opened.
candidates.mechanism: Two sub-key searches generate k² candidate pairs; exact top-k over their summed scores indexes independent learned value vectors, followed by sparse weighted retrieval. Product means Cartesian codebook, not elementwise feature multiplication.
candidates.osram_mapping: Form one bounded adapter descriptor from masked Local/Base/Gap and availability. Its internal lookup projection indexes a task-trained parameter table, then role-specific decoders return raw-slot residuals. No sample cache, missing-value reconstruction or persistent per-utterance state; OSRAM query tensors remain untouched.
candidates.substantive_difference: N3 retrieves current evidence neighbors recursively; Compositional Attention selects value-projection outputs; Perceiver compresses evidence into latent states; NetVLAD accumulates center residuals. PKM routes into an exact Cartesian-indexed learned parameter table with independently stored pair values. Must retain factorized search and pair-index values rather than use ordinary attention over a small prototype bank.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Sparse parameter specialization may separate distinct Local/Base/Gap agreement regimes without averaging all regimes through the same dense transform.
risks: Small data may leave most entries untrained. The source's large-capacity parameter-memory motivation has not been translated into a justified table size for these fixed roles.

Concrete suitability gap: a capacity-controlled small-table mapping must show why product-key allocation is needed instead of an ordinary bounded nonlinear transform; source scaling alone is not justification.
Lookup descriptors must never include labels or another utterance; unavailable raw slots are masked before descriptor construction and after decoding.

candidates.title: An Explicitly Relational Neural Network Architecture
candidates.source_evidence: Paper §2, Fig.1, Eqs.(1)–(7) inspected. Author notebook PrediNet4MultiTask: two global-context queries, shared keys, att1/att2, feature1/feature2, shared embed_entities, subtraction, then both selected positional descriptors concatenated (raw notebook lines 629–663). The task-id concatenation belongs to the subsequent task head and is not required by the central PrediNet module.
candidates.mechanism: Each head selects two entities with independently generated whole-input queries; both entities enter a relation map shared across heads; their projected difference and both bound entity identifiers form an ordered propositional record. Concatenate records before decoding.
candidates.osram_mapping: Five semantic roles become entities after dimension alignment. Replace image coordinates with fixed role identity descriptors carried through both selections. Both selectors mask unavailable slots. Generate adapter-internal queries from the masked five-role input, preserve shared predicate map, concatenate predicate records and decode slot residuals; no task IDs or extra labels.
candidates.substantive_difference: DAT aggregates relation-plus-sender-symbol messages for each receiver; PrediNet first binds two independently selected entities and emits shared-predicate records with both argument identities. Differential attention subtracts maps for denoising and discards argument bindings; keeping only a difference of weighted features would collapse this proposal toward that prior and is insufficient. NLM performs arity/quantifier inference rather than binding a fixed set of predicate arguments.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: An explicit Local-versus-Base or Base-versus-Gap predicate can retain which two sources disagree while sharing the comparator across role pairings.
risks: Soft entity mixtures may blur argument identity.
Two heads can collapse to the same pair.
Role identities are categorical metadata, not invented image geometry; preserve both bound identities and shared comparator to maintain the claimed distinction.

candidates.title: From Sparse to Soft Mixtures of Experts
candidates.source_evidence: Paper §2.1 Eqs.(1),(2), Algorithm 1 and §2.3 inspected. Author SoftRouter.__call__ lines 51–97 normalizes input/slot parameters, computes one logits tensor, dispatch softmax across input items and combine softmax across expert/slot axes. get_metrics line 113 returns zero auxiliary_loss; expert application is explicit in paper Algorithm 1. Local prior code inspected: meaningful_blocks_set_context.py _PerceiverCrossAttention/_PerceiverSelfAttention use shared FFN and separate attention projections; meaningful_input_representation.py _TokenLearnerFuser uses analysis-softmax, shared TransformerBlock, token-axis linear mixing and an independent synthesis-sigmoid; meaningful_blocks_grouping.py SlotAttentionGrouping uses shared GRU/MLP across slots.
candidates.mechanism: Compute D=softmax_over_tokens(XPhi), C=softmax_over_slots(XPhi); each independently parameterized expert transforms its dispatched mixed-input slots; reconstruct tokens as C times expert outputs. Both maps derive from the same normalized compatibility tensor.
candidates.osram_mapping: Apply masked dispatch to the five role vectors, execute several independent nonlinear experts on complete mixed-evidence slots, combine back to the same roles, then decode residuals before existing Flat. All routing groups contain one utterance only; no load-balancing loss.
candidates.substantive_difference: Verified distinction is mixed-input dispatch before independently parameterized expert execution, followed by tied-logit dual-axis reconstruction. Local SlotAttention shares GRU/MLP across slots; local Perceiver shares FFNs and uses separate decoder queries; local TokenLearner/Fuser uses a shared transformer and token-axis linear mixing, with independent synthesis logits. None implements the complete tied dispatch–independent expert–combine graph. Do not count changing only a gate or the number of latent slots.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Different experts may specialize in whole-evidence agreement patterns, rather than merely rescale one source.
risks: Use a small expert bank, e.g. three or four distinct nonlinear transforms; no long-sequence speed or giant-capacity argument applies to five roles.
Replacing expert functions by scalar gates or a shared MLP invalidates the proposal.
All experts can receive nearly identical mixtures; mask empty groups explicitly.

candidates.title: BASE Layers: Simplifying Training of Large, Sparse Models
candidates.source_evidence: Paper §3.1–3.2 and Eq.(2) inspected: maximum total token/expert affinity under equal capacities, auction assignment during training and greedy choice at inference. Author BaseLayer.forward, balanced_assignment, greedy_assignment and BaseSublayer.forward inspected. Code uses gated interpolation of expert output, while paper figure describes residual mixing; do not silently conflate those variants.
candidates.mechanism: Joint constrained assignment of all tokens to capacity-limited distinct expert networks; route, transform and invert the routing permutation. The coupled assignment, rather than the final scalar blend, is the proposed core.
candidates.osram_mapping: Candidate adapter would solve an assignment only over one utterance's active role tokens and run a small expert bank before decoding to original slots. Preserve the original OSRAM state and Flat. Never balance across batch utterances.
candidates.substantive_difference: BASE optimizes a linear token-to-expert allocation with fixed expert capacities, then executes expert transformations. Graph matching compares relational consistency between two evidence graphs; OTKE performs soft mass transport to supports; NPS selects a rule/entity pair without equal expert capacities. A top-1 independent gate would not qualify.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Capacity coupling could prevent every source from choosing the same transform and enforce complementary expertise without an auxiliary loss.
risks: Concrete mapping gap: variable active cardinalities 1–5 do not generally divide the expert count. An explicit mask-safe capacity policy must be defined; silently assigning unavailable placeholders violates scope.
Source train/test routing differs; migration must declare which policy is preserved.
Cross-utterance assignment and distributed token shuffling from the source are forbidden.

candidates.title: Reformer: The Efficient Transformer
candidates.source_evidence: Paper §2, Eqs.(4)–(6), Appendix A inspected: angular random-projection hashes, bucket sorting/chunking, multi-round union and repeated-pair correction. Author efficient_attention.py hash_vectors/hash_vecs and LSH attention source inspected; padding is given a separate bucket in hash_vectors lines 1736–1754.
candidates.mechanism: Random angular hashing constructs sparse neighborhoods; perform shared-QK attention within sorted buckets across multiple hash rounds and combine with correct normalization/duplicate handling. Hashing determines interactions, not a post-attention top-k gate.
candidates.osram_mapping: Five masked role vectors can be hashed directly, processed within same-utterance bucket neighborhoods, unsorted and decoded. Fixed random hashes are parameters/buffers, not a sample cache. No autoregressive context or OSRAM query modification.
candidates.substantive_difference: N3 repeatedly relaxes nearest-neighbor selection without replacement; DGCNN recomputes metric kNN edges; Reformer uses multi-hash collision neighborhoods and correction for repeated neighbor encounters. Neither prior has this routing algorithm.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Random content-dependent sparse neighborhoods may limit unrelated source interference; this is a regularization hypothesis, not a speed claim on five tokens.
risks: Very short sets make bucket singleton/all-in-one collapse likely.
Self-only fallback is required when no other available token shares a bucket.
Do not count reversible residual layers as a second method, or omit multihash/duplicate correction while retaining the paper name.

candidates.title: BiFormer: Vision Transformer with Bi-Level Routing Attention
candidates.source_evidence: Paper §3.2, Algorithm 1, Eqs.(3)–(7) inspected: pooled region graph, top-k region selection, gather all token keys/values from selected regions, then token attention plus local context convolution. Author TopkRouting.forward, KVGather and BiLevelRoutingAttention code inspected; default routing may detach region query/key tensors.
candidates.mechanism: Coarse region selection controls a second fine-token retrieval stage. Region selection and fine-token attention operate on different sets, and the whole chosen region's tokens remain available to fine retrieval.
candidates.osram_mapping: Possible role-as-region mapping would derive several sub-tokens per raw Local/Base/Gap vector, select evidence roles using pooled sub-token summaries, and retrieve fine sub-tokens only inside selected roles. Availability removes a role and all its children. Existing Flat is unchanged after decoding.
candidates.substantive_difference: This is coarse-to-fine selection over a region/token hierarchy, not recursive token-neighbor selection or composition of search/value heads. However, one token per role collapses the hierarchy to ordinary sparse attention, so that degenerate migration is not acceptable.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: First select useful evidence sources, then compare several facets inside them, reducing distractor subfeatures.
risks: Concrete mapping gap: input vectors lack genuine spatial regions or sub-token structure; learned splitting must be justified without pretending feature coordinates are image patches.
The original local depthwise spatial convolution has no natural role-space counterpart.
Remains pending until an explicit two-level mapping preserves the source mechanism rather than manufacturing token count.

candidates.title: Efficient Content-Based Sparse Attention with Routing Transformers
candidates.source_evidence: Paper §4.1 inspected: spherical clustering and EMA centroid update. Author utils.py cluster_items, online_kmeans and embedding_lookup inspected (lines 2710–2900). online_kmeans explicitly adds beta*e_loss in EMA mode and q_loss+beta*e_loss otherwise; these are commitment/codebook objectives absent from the paper's high-level summary.
candidates.mechanism: Cluster queries and keys with online centroids, gather fixed-size near-centroid neighborhoods, apply sparse attention and scatter results; source code learns routing with extra clustering losses.
candidates.osram_mapping: Same-utterance role clustering is technically possible, but faithful author training introduces an auxiliary objective prohibited here. Removing it is an unvalidated altered method, not automatic source-faithful admission.
candidates.substantive_difference: Clustering determines sparse attention support rather than pooled slot updates or residual descriptors; nevertheless source-faithful training fails the current task-loss boundary.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Content clusters might separate evidence regimes, but this rationale does not override the objective restriction.
risks: Auxiliary commitment/codebook loss violates scope.
EMA centroids aggregate training examples, so their distinction from prohibited external state would also need explicit treatment.
Do not misreport paper-only inspection as confirming a zero-auxiliary-loss implementation.

candidates.title: Parallelizing Linear Transformers with the Delta Rule over Sequence Length
candidates.source_evidence: Paper §2.2 and §3.1 inspected: retrieve old value S*k, erase its association and write beta*(v-S*k)*k^T. §3 supplies the generalized Householder/WY parallelization. Author DeltaNet layer and imports of chunk_delta_rule/fused_recurrent_delta_rule inspected; no local implementation was made.
candidates.mechanism: Associative matrix update S_next=S+beta*(v-S*k)*k^T, then a query read. Chunkwise execution accelerates the same recurrence.
candidates.osram_mapping: A new same-utterance recurrence could reset its state per call, but adding another delta-rule memory outside existing OSRAM would relocate an existing core rather than establish a new one. Replacing OSRAM writes/queries is explicitly out of scope.
candidates.substantive_difference: No qualifying distinction from the existing delta-rule memory is established. WY/chunk parallelization changes implementation efficiency, not the associative update; short evidence lists do not need the source long-sequence optimization.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Error-corrective associative storage is plausible in general, but cannot be sold as a new OSRAM fusion mechanism without a distinct permitted computation.
risks: Mechanism relocation is explicitly disallowed by the registry.
A Gated DeltaNet rename or modified scalar forgetting gate does not resolve duplication.
Parent audit identified the existing-memory collision; local OSRAM write equation was not fully re-audited in this lane.
